notes: "The RECORD DELIMITER clause may be specified only for variable-length records" is ENFORCED on both arms since kb/Work PB5844 (COBOL7599, FileControlBinder.ScreenRecordDelimiter, post-build because the record type is the file description entry's to say). The record type is FileModel.HasVariableLengthRecords, the one predicate the FORMAT clause's rule asks too: the RECORD clause's variable formats and the implied format 2 (Annex A.1 items 147 and 148, the implementor's answers to SR1's NOTE), or a LINE SEQUENTIAL file whose entry writes no format 1 RECORD clause (§2023:9.1.7.2), so the line sequential case the earlier decline feared to refuse is accepted. A format 1 clause ("Format 1 is used to specify fixed-length records", §2023:13.18.43.4 GR6) or no RECORD clause over fixed-length record descriptions is refused, whichever operand the clause names: the §2023:4.2.6 ¶3 licence not to diagnose syntax errors within unsupported syntax reaches only the declined STANDARD-1 phrase (§2 row 26), never the clause's placement, and the feature-name arm is provided (A.1 item 150). The same rule at COBOL-85 is §1985:VII.2.8.3 SR1, enforced by the same code; the edition picks the citations. retired-witness: conformance-test:DocumentedNonSupportWitnessTests.RecordDelimiterFeatureName_NamedNonSupportWarning_PinnedToSpec (kb/Work PB5844 provides the feature-name arm (BINARY-SEQUENTIAL, LINE-SEQUENTIAL), so the test that pinned its COBOL1778 decline is deleted; its successor DocumentedNonSupportWitnessTests.RecordDelimiterImplementorName_DrawsNoWarning pins the opposite)
